## TL;DR

The board already applies `sort=oldest|newest` and shows every phone-only status value (`attention`, `held`, `archived`, `human`, `all`) as a dashed "Ignored filter" chip, so none is dropped silently. This session I confirmed that wiring, found the branch's merge with main was still open, and ran the scoped check. The filter and browser suites pass at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The full test run had failures in agent-review, debugger-integration and preview-request; those files pass when run alone, so they look like load-dependent timeouts, but I have not proven that on an idle machine.

## Work and rationale

The task asks that each URL value be either applied or shown with a notice. I read `src/ui-app/src/lib/workQueueFilters.ts` first, because the task says to keep the ignored-value notice path there. It already does the work: `readWorkQueueSort` accepts only `newest` or `oldest`, `sortWorkQueueTasks` orders each column by `updated_at`, and `ignoredWorkQueueFilterChips` turns any non-board `status` into a notice. `WorkView.vue` applies the sort inside `visibleByStatus`, so it covers every column. `BoardQueueFilters.vue` renders the applied sort chip and the ignored chips in one bar.

I checked coverage rather than assuming it. A table-driven unit test in `src/ui-app/tests/work-queue-filters.test.ts` runs `attention`, `all`, `needs`, `held`, `archived`, `human` and `bogus` through the notice path. The headless WebKit fixtures in `src/ui-app/tests/work-filter-persistence-qa-browser.test.ts` check the sort chip and the status notice at 375, 768 and 1280 px, plus chip wrapping and the Clear control at each width. All 60 tests in those two files pass through `bun run test`.

I did not change any product code this session. Only the handoff blocker and the check outcome were new. `docs/qa/2026-11-filter-persistence-qa.md` already records the fix under "Behavior on the board".

## Approaches tried

I first ran the two filter test files with `bunx vitest run` directly. That failed on `.vue` import analysis because it skipped the repo's Vue plugin config. The repo wrapper, `bun run test -- <files>`, runs them correctly, so I used it for everything after that.

For the failed handoff I looked at git state. `MERGE_HEAD` exists, the merge message names `docs/qa/2026-11-filter-persistence-qa.md` and `src/ui-app/src/views/WorkView.vue` as conflicts, and neither file has unmerged paths or conflict markers. The merge is resolved in the index but not concluded.

I ran the scoped gate with `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. Build, format, lint and the docs and link checks passed. The tests step failed. I reran the failing files alone and they passed, then reran the tests step and it still failed with 6 tests across 4 files. I then started the full suite in the background to get the complete failure list. It was stopped at its background time limit before it finished, so I do not have a full list beyond the failures above.

## Challenges and blockers

The handoff is blocked by the open merge, not by the code. RepoOS's commit step reports `cannot do a partial commit during a merge` because the index has the merge result while `work/*.md` bookkeeping files are unstaged. The runner rules say not to run `git add` or `git commit`, so I did not conclude the merge. Someone with commit rights needs to conclude it, or let RepoOS do so after the merge is finished. Per AGENTS.md the `work/1260-*.md` copy should be main's copy in that merge; I did not verify that.

The scoped tests step is not green. The failing tests are agent-review (a 90-second timeout on partial output), debugger-integration (a 30-second timeout on the optimistic re-broadcast case) and preview-request (the sandboxed preview E2E). All of them pass when run alone. That is the pattern the repo's debugging notes describe for memory-pressure flakes, but I have not confirmed it on an idle machine, and nothing in this diff touches those code paths.

## Key learnings

Before rewriting a feature, check whether the branch already implements it. Here the code and tests were done in an earlier turn, and the remaining work was the merge and the check.

Run the repo's own test wrapper, not bare vitest. A file that imports `.vue` only works under the project config.

A merge that is resolved in the index but not concluded looks like a clean tree to a reader, but it blocks any partial commit. Check `MERGE_HEAD` before assuming the tree is clean.
